sections.hypothesis: Trend-vol-target on BTC, ETH and SOL earns more per unit of risk if it steps into cash on days the 4h regime model's last bar of the day is in its most volatile state: the 4h model sees volatile spells coming about 40 hours before the daily model (findings 23), early enough to step aside before the worst days rather than after them.
sections.rationale:
Economic reason: trend rules lose most in panicky, high-volatility markets that whip back and forth, where the trend signal turns late (Daniel and Moskowitz, Momentum Crashes, JFE 2016: crashes cluster in high-volatility panic states and are partly forecastable; indirect evidence, as it is cross-sectional momentum). Who pays: nobody pays you to be out; the claim is only that sitting out avoids losses the trend rule takes, net of the costs of leaving and coming back.

DISCLOSED: this is a second try at a rejected note, regime-filter-on-trend-vol-target-btc (rejected 2026-11-14: Sharpe 0.64 with the daily filter against 0.69 without, BTC 2021-05 to 2025-10). That note stays rejected. The new reason is a property measured afterwards, from a description rather than a trading result: findings 23 (2026-11-22, pre-holdout, no trials) found a 4h model of the same shape is volatile a median 40 to 44 hours before the daily model's volatile spells and called 82 to 100% of them, but 72 to 80% of its spells are false alarms. The daily filter failed because the plain rule already holds only 13% on volatile days (findings 8): by the time the daily model says volatile, trend-vol-target has mostly left. An earlier warning is the only way the filter could add something. The false alarms are the risk: the 4h model is volatile about 27% of the time against 14% for the daily one, so this filter steps out on many more ordinary days and pays a round trip each time.

Expected result, stated before running: more likely to fail than pass. Written after trend-vol-target's 2020-25 and holdout results were seen, and after findings 23.
sections.rules:
Implementation trend-vol-target-regime-4h at trend-vol-target's defaults: the plain weight, set to 0 on a day whose regime_volatile_4h is 1. That feature is the stored 4h fit's state for the 4h bar that closes at the day's close (opens 20:00 UTC), filtered, so known at the close the daily decision is made; a day without a 4h state keeps the plain weight. The 4h fit is kestrel.regimes.FAST_PRESET, findings 23's 4h model, fixed 2026-11-22 before this note: 3 states, inputs each 4h bar's log return and log 20-bar realised volatility, refitted at the start of each month on the year before (3 restarts, seed 0), stored by kestrel regimes <COIN> --interval 4h --save from 2017-08 to 2025-10 (data/regimes/4h/). Decide at the daily close, fill at the next open (00:00 UTC), like every daily backtest.

Markets and periods, from the first month every day has a 4h state (4h bars start 2020-01 for BTC and ETH, 2020-08 for SOL) to the holdout: BTCUSDT and ETHUSDT 1d 2020-12 to 2025-10; SOLUSDT 1d 2021-08 to 2025-10. 330 USDT, costs from kestrel.toml. Six runs, each once:
  kestrel backtest <COIN> --strategy trend-vol-target-regime-4h --research <this note> --interval 1d --start <start> --end 2025-10 --cash 330   (filter on)
  the same with --param regime_filter=0   (the plain rule on the same days: the comparison)
sections.falsification:
Adopted only if, on at least 2 of the 3 coins, against the plain rule on the same coin and period: (1) its Sharpe is higher; (2) its max drawdown is no deeper; and (3) its run's scorecard fails no test the plain rule's run passes (the tests a single run grades: edge against exposure-matched holding, deflated Sharpe, break-even cost, trades, drawdown). Only if all of that holds do walk-forward and the neighbouring-settings test follow, and those runs count as trials too. Otherwise the note is rejected (with Luke's say-so) and trend-vol-target stays as it is.

If adopted, it replaces nothing: the holdout is spent for BTC, ETH and SOL, so it can never get a holdout verdict. The only further evidence would be paper trading forward as its own accounts beside the plain ones. Run once; no settings change after the results are seen (a 2-state or a half-weight version would be a new note and new trials).
sections.parameters: fast_days 20, mid_days 60, slow_days 120, vol_days 30, target_vol_pct 50 (trend-vol-target's defaults); regime_filter 1 (on) or 0 (plain rule). The 4h model: FAST_PRESET (3 states, 20 bars, 1-year window, monthly refits, 3 restarts, seed 0). Nothing is tuned.
sections.costs: Each coin's costs as kestrel.toml sets them, the same as trend-vol-target's own runs (fee, half-spread and slippage on every fill). The filter adds a sale on stepping out and a purchase on stepping back in, and the 4h model's frequent false alarms make these much more common than with the daily filter; the no-trade band (2%) stops nothing when a whole position moves. Six runs, six trials (the plain-rule runs count too, as they always have).
